proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Energy Information Administration report levelized costs of electricity with the cost of backup or firming power for wind and solar shown as a separate component, work with FERC, NERC and RTOs to redefine reserve margins around dispatchable on-demand resources, make its federal subsidies report an annual or biennial base-program product, keep the International Energy Outlook objective and based on current law, and assess the case for privatization.

A new or recurring federal subsidies report (page 388)

review.mandate_note: Pages 387 and 388, as described in the record, recommend that EIA show firming or backup costs for wind and solar as a separate levelized cost component, work with FERC, NERC and RTOs to redefine reserve margins around dispatchable resources, make its federal subsidies report a regular product, keep the International Energy Outlook based on current law, and assess privatization. status_summary: No EIA action matching the firming-cost, reserve-margin, subsidy-report or privatization items was found. EIA's levelized cost paper for the Annual Energy Outlook 2026, released 2026-04-08, uses a value-cost ratio framework and does not mention firming or backup costs or reserve margins. EIA's latest federal subsidies report remains the edition released 2023-08-01, and the FY2027 DOE budget request for EIA seeks $135.37 million and does not mention firming costs, a subsidy report, reserve margins or privatization.
